Living near this establishment has become an ongoing frustration for the residents on this street.

The activity associated with the congregation regularly creates problems for the surrounding neighbourhood, including speeding, vehicles blocking the street, congestion, and visitors who can be intrusive toward residents. This is a residential street, yet there often seems to be very little consideration for the people who actually live here.

More recently, we have experienced break-ins in the neighbourhood. In at least some incidents, video surveillance appears to show individuals coming from or leaving the area around this establishment. I am not suggesting that the establishment or congregation was responsible, but this footage has understandably increased concerns among residents about the activity coming into and out of the area.

The issue isn't simply that people attend this establishment. It's the cumulative impact on the neighbourhood—traffic, speeding, blocked streets, intrusive behaviour, and now increased security concerns.

I believe the establishment needs to do more to manage the behaviour and traffic associated with its visitors and show greater consideration for the residents who live here.

reviews.name: Steffi Don
reviews.text:
A lecture on September 13, 2026 by Asifa Qadri focused largely on forgiveness, using the story of Thumamah ibn Uthal as an example.

She described Thumamah as an opponent of the Muslims who was cruel and had stopped the food supply, which led the Prophet to send horsemen to capture him and bring him to Medina. He was kept in the mosque for three days, where the Prophet questioned him each day. On the third day, the Prophet forgave him. Thumamah then went to a palm garden, bathed, returned to the mosque, and declared Islam.

Historical Concern
• Sahih al-Bukhari 4372 mentions the food supply issue happened after Thumamah had already become Muslim and gone to Makkah. Therefore, the narration does not support presenting the food-supply issue as the original reason for his capture.

• There is a gap in the narration between his release, bathing, returning to the mosque, and declaring Islam. Since he had been a captive, the narration does not tell us enough about what happened during that interval or what other circumstances influenced his decision.

• Therefore, the narration does not explicitly establish that he became Muslim because the Prophet forgave him. That is an interpretation, not a stated cause-and-effect explanation.

The speaker concluded her lecture with:

“Jo maaf nahi karta, uske dil mein badla hota hai. Agar badla lenge to badle ka anjaam dushmani hota hai, aur dushmani mein khoon kharaba hota hai. To maaf karo sabko.”

Concern About Forgiveness

• Not forgiving someone does not automatically mean seeking revenge. A person can reject revenge while still having a legitimate desire for justice and accountability.

• Forgiveness should be voluntary. It should not be imposed on or extracted from the person who was harmed.

• Forgiveness does not mean that wrongdoers should face no real-world consequences. Justice and forgiveness are separate principles. Legitimate justice can be pursued through lawful authorities and legal systems rather than personal revenge.

• Telling people to “forgive everyone” without emphasizing justice and accountability can make a community dysfunctional by discouraging victims from seeking legitimate justice and allowing wrongdoing to go unaddressed.

Religious and Community Responsibility

• When religious leaders receive disclosures of abuse, coercion, harassment, intimidation, or serious mistreatment, these should not be suppressed, shamed, terrorized, coerced, or reframed as simply a matter of forgiveness. Such matters should not be handled through informal cultural practices that allow the abuse to continue or lead to further abuse. Religious centres should formally report such disclosures to the appropriate authorities where required by law.

• Religious centres should verify that invited teachers meet the required Canadian licensing and certification requirements.

Canadian Accountability

Canada should establish a formal Canadian licensing and certification system for Islamic religious authorities who provide public religious instruction. Foreign qualifications or certifications should not automatically qualify someone to act as a religious authority in Canada. Canada should have its own standards and quality-control licensing exam in order to become a religious leader.

• The exam should cover religious knowledge, Canadian law, human rights, and the responsible real-life application of religious teachings in a manner consistent with Canadian law and human rights, including ensuring that religious teachings are not applied through coercion, intimidation, or social pressure.

• There should be ongoing government oversight and an independent complaint process; simple enough to be practically used.

• The government should ensure that religious centres and professionals follow reporting requirements properly, accurately, and honestly, rather than suppressing, shaming, terrorizing, coercing, minimizing, or misrepresenting reports of abuse.

Forgiveness and justice can coexist. One does not have to cancel each other out.

reviews.name: Tarannum S
reviews.text:
A wonderful masjid and a warm, welcoming community. One of the things I really appreciate is the wide range of educational programs for young children, including Quran classes, Sunday school, and both winter and summer camps. These programs provide children with a great opportunity to learn, build friendships, and stay connected to the masjid.

The masjid also does a great job bringing the community together through social activities, including potlucks twice a month and special events such as henna nights before Eid. These gatherings create a wonderful family-friendly atmosphere and help everyone feel connected.

Overall, it’s a beautiful place for worship, learning, and community. A great masjid for families and children!
